Mole Poblano with Rice

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 6Prep 45 minCook 2 hr

Mole Poblano is a rich, complex sauce made with a blend of chiles, spices, chocolate, and nuts, traditionally served over turkey or chicken. It is a signature dish during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, a major Mexican celebration honoring the Virgin Mary, where families gather to share this festive meal.

Ingredients

  • 3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
  • 3 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
  • 3 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
  • 1/4 cup sesame seeds (35 g), plus extra for garnish
  • 1/4 cup almonds (30 g)
  • 1/4 cup raisins (40 g)
  • 1 corn tortilla, torn into pieces
  • 2 slices white bread, crust removed and torn
  • 1 small onion, quartered
  • 3 cloves garlic
  • 1 medium tomato, chopped
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/2 teaspoon black peppercorns
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • 3 cups chicken broth (720 ml)
  • 1 ounce Mexican dark chocolate or bittersweet chocolate (28 g), chopped
  • Salt to taste
  • 6 bone-in chicken thighs
  • 2 cups long grain white rice (370 g)
  • 4 cups water (960 ml)
  • 1 tablespoon vegetable oil
  • Salt to taste

Method

  1. Toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about 2 minutes each side, being careful not to burn them.
  2. Place toasted chiles in a bowl and cover with hot water; soak for 20 minutes until softened.
  3. In the same skillet, toast sesame seeds, almonds, and raisins separately until golden and fragrant; set aside.
  4. Toast the torn tortilla pieces and bread slices in the skillet until crisp and golden.
  5. In the skillet, sauté onion, garlic, and tomato in 2 tablespoons vegetable oil until soft, about 5 minutes.
  6. Drain chiles and blend them with the sautéed vegetables, toasted nuts, seeds, raisins, tortilla, bread, cinnamon stick, thyme, oregano, cloves, peppercorns, and 1 cup chicken broth until smooth.
  7. Heat the remaining 2 cups chicken broth in a large pot; add the blended mole sauce and cook over low heat, stirring frequently, for about 1 hour.
  8. Add chopped chocolate and salt to taste; stir until chocolate is melted and sauce is thickened.
  9. In a separate pot, heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil; add rice and toast for 2 minutes.
  10. Add 4 cups water and salt to taste; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 18 minutes or until rice is tender.
  11. Meanwhile, cook chicken thighs by boiling or roasting until fully cooked and tender.
  12. Serve the chicken topped with mole poblano sauce, garnished with sesame seeds, accompanied by the white rice.

Tips

  • For a smoother mole, strain the sauce through a fine sieve before cooking.
  • If Mexican chocolate is unavailable, use bittersweet chocolate with a small pinch of cinnamon added.
  • Mole improves in flavor if made a day ahead and reheated gently.
